body:
MEASURED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-24, Kobo Clara BW firmware 4.45.23792, against the
deployed server, on a probe book that held zero annotations at baseline.

## What was observed

A highlight that was **on no device snapshot** and is **`hidden=1` on the CWNG
server** was restored to the reader by a re-download, rendered on the page, and
marked `Hidden='false'` locally.

Annotation `789e11f0-6511-462e-9614-f465fef39592` (`Vivek `, created
2026-08-24T04:42:20Z during an earlier probe, CWNG row id 645, `hidden=1`):

    device snapshots t0, t1, t1b, t2, t4   row ABSENT   (5 consecutive pulls)
    after the re-download (t5)             row PRESENT  Hidden='false'
                                           SyncTime = 2026-08-24T22:37:48Z
                                                      (the re-download's sync)

It is drawn on the page, photographed alongside two live highlights, so this is
not a hidden-row artefact: the reader sees a highlight they no longer have.

## Where it came from, and where it did not

**Not from CWNG's writeback.** [OBSERVED] `config_kobo_two_way_annotation_sync`
is `0`; book 540's `kobo_annotation_book_state` is `authority_status='unseeded'`
with `current_etag` NULL; there are **zero** `annotation_device_state` rows for
this annotation. `cps/readingservices.py` contains no `hidden` handling at all.

**From upstream Kobo, through our proxy.** [OBSERVED in source]
`handle_annotations` at `cps/readingservices.py:468` documents and implements
exactly this: *"GET: proxied directly to Kobo."* The PATCH path captures locally
**and** proxies upstream, so every annotation the device ever authored on a
sideloaded book has also been stored in Kobo's cloud. On the authoritative fetch
that follows a re-download, Kobo returns the set **it** holds, and CWNG passes it
through unfiltered.

## Why this matters beyond one probe row

The proxy is transparent in both directions, so **Kobo's copy outranks both the
device's and CWNG's.** Any annotation the user deleted on the device, or that
CWNG has soft-deleted, is re-delivered whenever the device next fetches
authoritatively — and `F-0b66d7` already established that a device-side deletion
only reaches the server when a later annotation change in the **same book**
carries it out. A deletion that never found a carrier is still live in Kobo's
cloud, waiting for the next re-download.

Composed with `F-5ff379` (a `last_modified` bump de-downloads the book) and the
`mark_book_modified` call sites — ordinary metadata edits, cover changes, fetched
metadata, format conversion, not just the KEPUB repair task — the user-visible
sequence is:

    user deletes a highlight
      -> deletion finds no same-book carrier, never reaches Kobo   [F-0b66d7]
      -> anyone edits that book's metadata                          [OBSERVED]
      -> device drops its downloaded copy                           [OBSERVED]
      -> user reopens the book, it re-downloads                     [OBSERVED]
      -> the deleted highlight is back, drawn on the page           [OBSERVED]

## What this means for the two-way sync design

`notes/KOBO-TWO-WAY-ANNOTATION-SYNC-DESIGN.md` treats CWNG as the authority once
a book is seeded. This finding says the **unseeded** path is not inert: it is an
active resurrection channel we currently proxy verbatim. Seeding a book does not
retire it unless the seeded path also stops proxying the GET. Section 11 should
state which side wins when Kobo's set and CWNG's set disagree, because today the
answer is "Kobo, silently".

## Not established

- Why Kobo still held this row. Two candidates — the deletion never reached Kobo,
  or it reached Kobo and was ignored — need different fixes. Distinguishing them
  needs the full PATCH/GET bodies on the wire, which is precisely what the
  exchange capture on **#1816** records. This is a concrete argument for landing
  that instrument.
- Whether an authoritative fetch happens on any trigger other than a re-download.
- Whether a note (`Add Note`) resurrects the same way as a bare highlight.

## Side observation, same run

The book's reading progress read **2% Read** before the cycle and **1% Read**
after. Not investigated; recorded so a later session does not treat it as new.

---

# CONTROLLED FOLLOW-UP, same night — the causal story above is RETRACTED

The section above explains the resurrection with F-0b66d7's carrier model: the
deletion never found a same-book carrier, so Kobo never heard about it. **That
explanation was tested and it failed.** The observation stands; the mechanism I
attached to it does not.

## The test, and the prediction registered before running it

On the same probe book, with a built-in control:

| row | its deletion | predicted after a re-download |
|---|---|---|
| `Vivek`, `Shandas`, `chronicling` | rode out on a carrier | stay gone |
| carrier `ba00dd26` | had **no** carrier behind it | **comes back** |

Establishing the setup first: deleting all three left three tombstones
(`Hidden='true'`, `SyncTime` NULL) exactly as F-0b66d7 describes; authoring one
new highlight in the same book and syncing **cleared all three outright**, which
is a clean second confirmation of the carrier model for *upload*.

## Result — 3 of 4, and the one that failed is the control

    delete WAS carried  -> Vivek, Shandas, chronicling : STAYED GONE   (predicted)
    delete NOT carried  -> carrier ba00dd26            : ALSO GONE     (REFUTED)

Device ended at **31 Bookmark rows, exactly the baseline**, after a completed
de-download / re-download cycle.

So deletions that reach Kobo stick — **including one with no carrier behind it.**
"The deletion never reached Kobo" is therefore not a sufficient explanation for
the original resurrection, and it is withdrawn as the leading hypothesis.

⚠️ One transient reading nearly became a false confirmation: mid-cycle the
carrier briefly read `Hidden='false'`, `SyncTime` set, which looks exactly like a
resurrection. It was the re-download still in flight — `IsDownloaded` was still
`false` and the count still 4. **Only the completed cycle is evidence.** An
earlier check in this session read the pre-cycle state and scored the prediction
against it; that reading was wrong and is why the cycle is now scored only on
`IsDownloaded='true'`.

## What remains ESTABLISHED, and it is the part worth acting on

Strip the causal speculation and a solid, checkable fact is left:

**CWNG's `annotation.hidden = 1` has no effect on what the reader sees.**

- [OBSERVED] Annotation `789e11f0` was `hidden=1` in CWNG's `app.db` and was
  delivered to the device and drawn on the page.
- [OBSERVED in source] `handle_annotations` (`cps/readingservices.py:468`)
  proxies the annotations GET straight to Kobo. CWNG never serves the set, so a
  CWNG-side soft delete is invisible to the device by construction.
- [OBSERVED] It was not our writeback: two-way sync off, book `unseeded`, zero
  `annotation_device_state` rows.

That matters for anything that soft-deletes: an operator or a task that hides an
annotation in CWNG will believe it is gone, and the reader will still see it.
Whatever §11 decides about authority, **hiding a row in our database is not a
deletion the user experiences**, and no UI should imply otherwise.

## Genuinely still open

- Why Kobo held `789e11f0` at all. Its device-side history is unknown — it may
  never have been deleted by a gesture; it may have been removed from the device
  by other means while Kobo kept its copy. Nothing in tonight's data settles it.
- Whether a pending, un-uploaded tombstone can be overwritten by an incoming GET
  before it uploads. That is the race worth testing next, it is the one that
  would lose a real user's deletion, and it needs the wire bodies from **#1816**.


---

## CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-28 (OBSERVED on hardware, fw 4.46.23836) — the re-download GET is proxied to Kobo, and Kobo holds a copy because CWNG forwards PATCHes

Why a CWNG-side `hidden=1` came back drawn on the reader (the "genuinely open" question above):

1. `handle_annotations` forwards every annotation PATCH upstream, owned books included (#1923). So
   Kobo's cloud holds a copy of each owned book's device-authored annotations.
2. A CWNG-side soft delete is never forwarded, so Kobo's copy keeps the row.
3. When the device re-downloads the book (tonight: after #1925 de-downloaded it), it issues
   `GET …/annotations?limit=100` directly — not via `checkforchanges` — and CWNG proxies that GET
   to Kobo. Kobo answers from its copy: a **200** hands the deleted row back (this finding); a
   **304** makes Nickel replace the book's local set with empty (§6p: 8 rows lost on a real book).

Containment covers only the `checkforchanges` route. Fix: #1923 — owned books' PATCH and GET are
answered locally (design Option B; §6g/§6o prove Nickel adopts and echoes a CWNG ETag).
title: CWNG's hidden=1 never reaches the reader, and the re-download GET proxied to Kobo hands the deleted row back (cause of the resurrection: #1923)
